rule_level_problems.problem: Page reaches 'Diagnose diabetes' only after 'No' to the urgent-signs box and 'No ketones'; the rule requires no ketonuria but not absence of urgent signs. A patient with glucose >= 11.1, symptoms and drowsiness gets both Urgent and probable Diabetes mellitus, which is clinically harmless.

Glucose is expressed as 'Blood glucose status' (observable entity); 'Blood glucose concentration' (observable entity) also exists. Correctness depends on which concept VHA records the routine glucose vital under. This checker could not verify that.

summary: Red-box triage logic is largely captured: hypoglycaemia (< 3, or < 4 with known diabetes) as probable and Urgent, the glucose >= 11.1 danger-sign box as Urgent, ketonuria as Urgent, and diabetes probable from random >= 11.1 with footnote-8 symptoms. The most consequential defects are 'Confusion' mapped to Clouded consciousness (a closer concept exists) and dehydration encoded as one concept without the footnote-7 signs (BP < 90/60, pulse >= 100 etc.). 'Type 1 diabetes likely if < 35' and impaired fasting glucose / fasting-glucose diabetes are unencoded because the language cannot express age in years or a fasting value.
